source_quality.notes: pages 11, 13 and 14 lost from the text layer; equations read from the raster

task_reconstruction: Measure the effect of the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse on commuters and non-commuters, site two new bus routes on a three-layer network, and propose an orange metro line.

section_map.summary: summary of the collapse, the bus layers and the metro line
background, the collapse, and the four steps
three assumptions and the notation table
the cleaning of names, outliers and abbreviations
the split into commuters and non-commuters and the closeness centrality
the three-layer bus network and the two new routes
the least-time routing and the density fit
the sensitivity test, the strengths and the weaknesses

contributions.summary: commuters and non-commuters recovered from the daily and weekday averages
closeness centrality compared on the highway graph with and without the bridge
bus stations scored and cut into core, bridge and outer layers
the metro's effect read as the gap between actual and fitted bus density

dependency_graph.relation: the distances feed the closeness centrality
the road graph carries the stations the score ranks
the layer speeds and the segment lengths feed the least-time routing

assumptions.summary: every vehicle runs at the speed limit of its layer
commuters travel only on weekdays and non-commuters are the same all week
any two nodes are joined by a path

data_and_preprocessing.summary: 354420 missing road names filled from the matching road code
9953 edges with three or more road codes dropped
two-road edges assigned by comparing three slopes
abbreviated road names expanded to full forms

models.summary: layered graph with travel time and flow conservation
weighted shell score cut into three bus layers
least-time routing and a quadratic density fit

verification.summary: closeness compared for 39 nodes with and without the bridge
four functional forms fitted and the quadratic kept
the grid refined from 2400 metres to 120 and the gain held

results_trace.summary: commuter flow rises on the harbour crossing while non-commuter flow falls
the links between the core and the bridge layer rise
the largest time savings fall in the suburbs

writing_logic.summary: the summary gives one block to each task
four steps are counted out before the models
each benefit is addressed to one named group
the close grants the base and then names what remains

language_observations.summary: opens on the closure cutting off a vital route
the coefficient is read by a greater-than-one rule
each benefit begins with the group it serves
the close opens with an although concession

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 5 draws the layered road network
Figures 9 and 10 plot the impact coefficient and rank the roads
Figure 12 shows the histogram the three layers are cut from

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: addressing each benefit to a named group matches a stakeholder brief
owning the flat growth and the subjective cuts reads as honest rather than weak

weaknesses.summary: the impact coefficient is drawn but never written as a formula
the counts are assumed to grow steadily
the model stays on the highways and misses the local roads
the layer cuts may rest on judgement

independent_extensions.summary: recover two traveller groups from a daily average and a weekday average
read one network's effect on another as the gap between actual and fitted density

unresolved_questions: the impact coefficient is drawn in a figure and never written as a formula
the quadratic fit is reported with no goodness of fit
the two layer cut points are read off the histogram and not derived
the threshold of three road codes is stated and not justified
the point-of-interest weights are stated and not fitted
